                                               FOREWORD
Legal reasoning is the backbone of success in CLAT and other law entrance exams. As one of the most interesting
and important subjects in law entrance tests, it has likely seen the most variations among all CLAT subjects.

Over the past few years, the number of Legal Reasoning, Legal Knowledge, and Assertion-Reason questions has
fluctuated significantly. From CLAT 2011 to 2019, the exam primarily featured Legal Reasoning questions.
However, CLAT 2012 and 2015 defied expectations by including a large number of Current Legal Knowledge
questions, with only a handful of Legal Reasoning questions. CLAT 2017 and 2018 surprised candidates with legal
maxims, statement-conclusion questions, and a variety of other formats. Post-CLAT 2019, the pattern shifted to
passage-based questions, but the level of difficulty and question types continued to surprise aspirants. CLAT 2023
featured moderate yet lengthy passages based on Current Legal Knowledge, while CLAT 2024 relied more on
Current Legal Knowledge-based passages. CLAT 2025, on the other hand, included more static topic-based passages
followed by direct questions. In CLAT 2026 the Consortium shifted to passages based on current legal knowledge
as well as Constitutional Law, the more surprising element was the application of extra-legal knowledge. While
many questions could be answered through a clear understanding of the passage, some required prior legal
knowledge, adding an additional layer of complexity.

The aim of this RSM is to provide comprehensive practice and enhance the reasoning skills of our Performers’ Batch
students. This module includes theme-based assignments and mixed practice sheets for Legal Reasoning in CLAT
as well as OLET (AILET and SLAT).


Happy Learning!
